---
title: "Drive on Start + Void"
description: "Native Drive Worker profiles, the sealed Cloudflare artifact, and the cutover and Vercel rollback packet."
updatedAt: "2026-11-09"
audience: developers
---

Drive (`apps/drive`) runs on TanStack Start, Vite+ and Void behind
[`@tuturuuu/start-bridge`](/build/devops/start-bridge). The Next.js build
(`build:legacy`) and the Vercel project stay in place until the cutover has been
stable, so the canonical host keeps a one-step route back.

## Worker profiles

| Profile | Selected by | Worker | Vars |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Staging (default) | no profile variable | the staging Worker name | `src/start-candidate/staging-policy.ts`; the build refuses a non-staging value |
| Production | `VITE_DRIVE_NATIVE_PROFILE=production` | `tuturuuu-drive` | `cloudflare/production-profile.json` |

Neither profile declares routes, custom domains, `workers_dev` or
`preview_urls`. The hostname is attached at cutover by the release operator.

The production Worker answers every request with a refusal until
`NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_URL`, `NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_PUBLISHABLE_KEY`,
`SUPABASE_SECRET_KEY` and `TUTURUUU_APP_COORDINATION_SECRET` are present
(`cloudflare/required-bindings.ts`). Names only are recorded here; values stay in
the secret store. Hosts other than the canonical Drive host answer `404`.

## Build and artifact

`drive-cloudflare-artifact.yaml` runs on `ready-for-ci` pull requests and by
manual dispatch. It builds with `bun run --cwd apps/drive build:cloudflare`,
records the emitted configuration receipt, and runs
`node --test apps/drive/cloudflare/cutover.runtime.mjs` against the emitted
Worker in workerd. On manual dispatch it seals the output with
`scripts/ci/drive-native-artifact.py` and uploads `drive-native-<source SHA>`
(7 days). The workflow never deploys.

Do not run `build:cloudflare` on a shared development machine; use the workflow.

## Cutover packet

| Item | Value |
| --- | --- |
| Worker | `tuturuuu-drive` |
| Route | `drive.tuturuuu.com/*` attached by the operator; no other host |
| Static assets binding | `ASSETS` (`dist/client`, `run_worker_first`) |
| Build command | `VITE_DRIVE_NATIVE_PROFILE=production bun run --cwd apps/drive build:cloudflare` |
| Secrets (names) | `NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_URL`, `NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_PUBLISHABLE_KEY`, `SUPABASE_SECRET_KEY`, `TUTURUUU_APP_COORDINATION_SECRET` |
| Central API origin | `INTERNAL_WEB_API_ORIGIN=https://tuturuuu.com` |
| Prior Vercel deployment | record the immutable deployment ID and URL of the `drive` Vercel project before the switch |
| Data | no database writes and no migrations |

### Switch

1. Record the source SHA, the sealed artifact name and the Vercel deployment ID.
2. Provision the four secrets on `tuturuuu-drive`, then deploy the sealed output.
3. Verify on the Worker before attaching the route: smoke below with the
   Worker's own address.
4. Attach `drive.tuturuuu.com` to the Worker (a proxied route in front of the
   still-valid Vercel origin where possible).

### Smoke

```bash
# Anonymous protected route redirects to /login; no 5xx
curl -sI https://drive.tuturuuu.com/00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000001 | head -5
# Login page renders
curl -s -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}\n' https://drive.tuturuuu.com/login
# Build identity matches the accepted SHA
curl -s https://drive.tuturuuu.com/api/build-info
# Foreign host is refused
curl -s -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}\n' -H 'Host: untrusted.invalid' https://drive.tuturuuu.com/login
```

Expected: a `30x` to `/login`, `200`, the accepted commit, and `404`.

### Rollback

- **Triggers:** a 5xx rate above 1% or an authentication failure loop for 5
  minutes, any cross-host response, or any storage permission regression.
- **Action:** remove the Worker route (or repoint the mapping) so
  `drive.tuturuuu.com` resolves to the recorded Vercel deployment again. Never
  rebuild on the rollback path.
- **Data:** a route rollback changes no stored files or metadata.
- **Stability:** keep the Vercel project and domain for 14 consecutive stable
  days before decommissioning, which is a separate approval.
